note: Florence County campground on quiet West Bass Lake south of Florence, with a sandy beach, boat launch and pavilion. Sites are 20x30 to 50x50 ft. ATVs may ride to and from the adjoining trail system. --Claude
summary: County booking page + 6 site pages + reservation policy PDF + 2024 map read. Now RESERVATION ONLY online (stored reservable false / fcfs always were derived and wrong): $25 + $10 reservation fee, Friday 2-night / holiday 3-night minimum, 14-night max. 29 electric sites (no amperage posted), no water at sites, shower house + pit toilets, no dump. Camping allowed year-round (water off mid-Oct to early May). PIN moves ~815 m. Not waterfront kept. Phone null -> 715-528-3207.
flags: PIN: stored 45.77280,-88.32397 is a forest road ~815 m south-east of the park -> 45.7768,-88.3328 (centre of the site loop; Google's 'West Bass Lake Park and Campground' pin 45.7780,-88.3314 is the day-use area).

BOOKING: stored reservable false / fcfs always (derived from old note prose) are wrong - the county now says 'West Bass Campground are reservation only' and every site is bookable at florencecountyparks.com.

WATERFRONT: 'not waterfront' kept. The loop's west sites (about 13-26) lie ~40-75 m from West Bass Lake through continuous pine/hardwood woods; the 2024 map shows no site at the shore. No site earns lakefront; a view through the trees isn't evidenced.
ELECTRIC: every site has electric ('Electricity?: Yes' and 'electricity to all sites') but no amperage is posted - hookups.electric left unknown.
PHONE: null -> 715-528-3207 (Florence County Forestry and Parks, from the reservation policy).

OHV: ATVs/UTVs may ride from the campground to the adjoining trail system (every site page: 'ATV/UTV Trail Access?: Yes') - a general county campground with ATV access, not a staging camp. Keep; reviewer informed.
SEASON: year-round camping allowed with no services November-April; written year_round true with the shut-off in season.note.
SITE SIZES: 20x30 ft (site 20) to 50x50 ft (site 1) - all fit a 23-ft rig; not written as max_rig_ft since they are pad dimensions, not posted limits.
